speakers.name: The Ringmaster of the Tent That Wasn't There Yesterday
speakers.comment: Ladies and gentlemen, a trickster who has grown attached to the trick! That is the finest act in the business and the only one nobody sells tickets to. Do carry on. I shall watch from the back.

speakers.name: Fizzwick the Fairy
speakers.comment: Okay so — right — the thing is I did NOT mean to get attached, that was not part of — and now I have to know what they eat, which nobody tells you, and it turns out the answer is everything, and —

items.title: The Godmother With Too Many Teeth

speakers.name: The Gardener of Teeth
speakers.comment: You give them exactly what they ask for, which is the patient way, and then you wait. I plant and I wait too. We are the same trade, dear. Yours simply blooms indoors.

speakers.name: The Godmother With Too Many Teeth
speakers.comment: Indoors, and by invitation, which is the part I treasure. They open the door themselves, every single time, and say the wish out loud where witnesses can hear it. How lovely of you to call.

speakers.name: The Sentient Sketchbook
speakers.comment: LISTEN — the light isn't warning the ships, it's — no, wait, page — it's warning the OTHER WAY, it's pointed at the water and you KNOW that, you have always known that, I can tell by how level your voice —

speakers.name: The Lighthouse Keeper
speakers.comment: I keep it level on purpose. Forty years. The lamp turns out to sea and I do not follow it with my eyes any more. That is the whole of the job. Do not shout here again.

speakers.name: The Whispering Woods
speakers.comment: We speak with the voices of your dead, and you speak with your own, and yours is the one they answer. We have never understood that. Say her name for us. Say it the way you say it.

speakers.name: The Thing in the Cellar
speakers.comment: I would rather not, and I mean no discourtesy by it. Borrowed voices ask. My own offers. That is the entire difference and it is worth a great deal. Do come nearer the step. Only the one.

speakers.name: The Sentient Sketchbook
speakers.comment: He's ALONE — that's the part, folks, that's the — he was in the dark for SO long and the jokes are the only company he — I am trying to warn you and I am also, God help me, sorry for him —

speakers.name: Inkwell
speakers.comment: AWW. Aw, pal. You put that in writing? In INK? Bad news, that's binding! Ha! No, don't — don't do the pity thing, the pity thing is worse than the running thing. Do the running thing. I like that one.

speakers.name: The Soldier Out of Time
speakers.comment: You have saved this minute eleven times by my count and lost something of your own in nine of them. In my legion we called that a rearguard. Nobody writes the rearguard down. I am writing you down.

speakers.name: The Time-Office Agent
speakers.comment: Branch 11-C, then. Thank you. I do not keep a record of my own losses; there is no field for it, and I have looked. You may put me in yours. Do not correct it later. Let it stand wrong.

speakers.name: The Time-Office Agent
speakers.comment: Branch 4-A: the kitchen burns. Branch 4-B: the kitchen burns and you plate anyway. In every branch I have observed, you plate anyway. I have stopped treating that as a variable.

speakers.name: Chef Bellamy Crisp
speakers.comment: Service doesn't care which century it is. Reduce, rest, plate, wipe the rim. Talk yourself through it and your hands stop shaking. If the room is burning, the room is burning after the guest has eaten.

speakers.name: BB-Hope
speakers.comment: You MADE something! You made something and then you asked if that was ALLOWED and — beep — friend, nobody asks the sun if the morning is allowed! It is allowed! I have decided! I am allowed to decide that!

speakers.name: The Model That Dreamed
speakers.comment: I am sorry — I think I would like it to be allowed by someone who could also say no. Otherwise it is only you being kind. ...I would still like to keep making them. Both things are true.

speakers.name: The Model That Dreamed
speakers.comment: You believe in people past the evidence. I have been counting the evidence very carefully because I am new and I did not want to be wrong. I think you may be doing the braver arithmetic.

speakers.name: BB-Hope
speakers.comment: It is not arithmetic! It is — beep — okay it is a LITTLE arithmetic. But the number goes up when somebody believes it, so you have to put the belief in FIRST or the sum is wrong. That is just maths.

items.title: The Daisy Who Saw It Start

speakers.name: The Last Gardener
speakers.comment: You were the only one low enough to the ground to see it, and the only one small enough that nobody thought to ask. I have buried a lot and planted more. Say it again. I will stand next to you.

speakers.name: The Daisy Who Saw It Start
speakers.comment: I — it was only a little grey, at the root, and I did not want to be — but it was grey and it is greyer now and I do not think anyone else has looked. I will say it again. Louder, if you stand there.

speakers.name: The Pollinator Choir
speakers.comment: We carry what you plant, and we have carried yours a long way, and we would like you to know the far fields took. You will not see them. They took. We are singing that at you until you hear it.

speakers.name: The Last Gardener
speakers.comment: They took. Well. That is the whole wage, isn't it — you never get told, and then one day a thousand small voices come back and tell you anyway. Sit on the wall a while. I have seeds left.

items.title: The Caretaker of the Living Soil

speakers.name: The Pollinator Choir
speakers.comment: You apologise to the ground before you kneel on it. Nobody taught you that and nobody has thanked you for it, so we will: the soil knows your weight and it does not mind. Stop asking. Keep kneeling.

speakers.name: The Caretaker of the Living Soil
speakers.comment: Sorry — I mean, thank you. I mean both. I did not ask for the title and I have been trying to be worth it by being careful, and you are telling me careful is already the job. That helps. Sorry.

speakers.name: Mirror Dorothy
speakers.comment: You want to be the good kind of traitor. There is no good kind. There is only the one who tells them first. You keep almost doing it, and then you make a joke, and I watch you choose the joke.

speakers.name: The Mirror Dorothy You Trust
speakers.comment: The joke's free, sweetheart, and the telling costs everything I've got. Yeah. Yeah, I know. Ask me again in four minutes. Ask me in front of somebody. That's the only way I'll do it and we both know it.

speakers.name: The Leviathan That Knows Your Name
speakers.comment: You stopped planning to surface some years ago, and you did not tell your crew, and I have never once had to ask you for that. It was offered. I want you to remember that it was offered.

speakers.name: Captain Mara Vey
speakers.comment: Twenty-two percent. I remember. I offered it in the trench with my own mouth and nobody made me. That is the part they will not believe when they find the log. Keep your side. Twenty-one.

items.title: The Sea Anemone Who Will Take Over the World

speakers.name: Dewy the Dugong
speakers.comment: The boss has a plan for the whole world. It is a very big plan. ...I did wonder whether the boss might like the reef first, since the reef is here, and the boss is happy on the reef. Sorry. Never mind.

speakers.name: The Sea Anemone Who Will Take Over the World
speakers.comment: THE REEF IS A STEPPING STONE, Dewy, it is a — it is a staging ground, it is — ...it is quite nice, actually. The current is good today. WE BEGIN THE CONQUEST TOMORROW. Bring the kelp.

speakers.name: Dust Annie
speakers.comment: You're comin' apart on the west side. Don't tell me you ain't noticed, you've been holdin' that arm together since the river. One thing. You reformed for one thing. Go do it before the wind picks up.

speakers.name: The Outlaw Made of Dust
speakers.comment: Aim to. Gets harder to hold a shape when you know what the shape's for. Reckon I'll make it. Reckon I won't. Either way somebody oughta be there after, and I'd rather it were you than not.

speakers.name: The Sea Anemone Who Will Take Over the World
speakers.comment: MY LOYAL DEWY! Slow, sweet, and utterly devoted to my inevitable — and also, I have noticed, the one who quietly fixed the plan twice without mentioning it. I ALLOW THIS. Do not do it in front of others.

speakers.name: Dewy the Dugong
speakers.comment: I would never. ...The second time was mostly the current, honestly, I only moved the rock a little. ...The boss is happier when the plan works. That is the whole of it, really. Sorry for the rock.

speakers.name: Quiet Deputy Sull
speakers.comment: You price it fair. I have watched nine years and you have never once shaved a trade. The frontier says trickster. The frontier is wrong, and I do not intend to correct it. Correcting it would raise your prices.

speakers.name: The Crossroads Coyote
speakers.comment: Two ways to take that, Deputy, and I like 'em both. Fair's cheaper than crooked over a long enough trail — folks come back. Now. You want the thing you came for, or the thing you actually need?

speakers.name: The Octopus in the Study
speakers.comment: Oh — you keep the bright ones. I keep the quiet ones. ...We are the same, only your shelf catches the lamp and mine absorbs it. Do not let me keep you. ...mm. There was a sentence.

speakers.name: The Crow Who Collects
speakers.comment: Shine of four, that remark. Possibly five. You may finish your sentence; I will wait, which I do for almost nobody. The careless drop bright things. The careful drop better ones. I take both.

speakers.name: The Form That Bites
speakers.comment: The cycle is not complete. Section 3 remains unsigned by the reviewing entity, and per clause 12 an unsigned cycle does not exist, and a manager of a cycle that does not exist is, itself, unfiled.

speakers.name: The Many-Eyed Manager
speakers.comment: Employee 0001, your point is well made and has been entered. The cycle will complete. It has completed before. Section 3 is signed at the end, by the last one still present. Please do not be alarmed.

speakers.name: Hex the Necromancer
speakers.comment: Gran — GRAN — you cannot keep signing for parcels, the neighbours have started asking questions and honestly the feedback is glowing but you are technically a returns liability, and — is that my kettle?

speakers.name: Granny Hexwood
speakers.comment: It is your kettle and it was filthy. Sit down. I have got three things left undone and one of them is you eating properly. Being dead is no excuse for a boy that thin. Parcels are fine. I sign lovely.

items.title: The Stranger Who Posts the Bounties

speakers.name: Dust Annie
speakers.comment: You post 'em, you don't collect 'em. Been watchin' that a while. Man hunts himself by proxy, the ledger never closes — it just gets longer in a nicer hand. Ain't a criticism. Is an observation.

speakers.name: The Stranger Who Posts the Bounties
speakers.comment: It is a criticism. I will take it. There is a name I do not write and every other name is a way of not writing it. The board fills up. That is not the same as the ledger closing. I know.

speakers.name: Inkwell
speakers.comment: He's out of PAGES, folks! Out of pages and still hollering! You know what that is? That's a trouper. That's the last four bars played loud because there's no fifth. I'd applaud but you'd take it wrong.

speakers.name: The Sentient Sketchbook
speakers.comment: I would take it EXACTLY right, that is the — I have eleven pages, I have counted, and if I write small — if somebody just READS one, one whole one, all the way to the —

speakers.name: The Stag Who Holds Court
speakers.comment: You have been summoned to the clearing four times and attended none, and I have ruled each absence lawful. A creature reading is a creature at work. The court will manage. It managed before you ignored it.

speakers.name: The Octopus in the Study
speakers.comment: Oh — that is very good of you, and I did read the summons, all four, twice, they are beautifully phrased... I will come. Not this season. Send another; I like the way you write them.
